title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Page headed '4)', in the series on the Teichmüller modular groups T_{g,n}. Here T_{1,1} = SL(2,Z), the mapping class group of the once-punctured torus.

(1) The figure shows the upper half-plane D. The hatched region is the triangle bounded by Re τ = 0, Re τ = 1/2 and the unit circle, with vertices i, j = e^{iπ/3} and the cusp at ∞. This is the (2,3,∞) triangle, a fundamental domain for PGL(2,Z), and half of the usual one for PSL(2,Z).

(2) Fixed generators:
- ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]]: its Möbius action is τ ↦ 1/(1−τ), which fixes j = e^{iπ/3}. One has ρ^3 = ω = −1.
- σ = [[0,1],[-1,0]]: its Möbius action is τ ↦ −1/τ, which fixes i. One has σ^2 = ω and σ^{-1} = ωσ.
- So ρ has order 6 and generates the isotropy group of j in SL(2,Z). σ has order 4 and generates the isotropy group of i. This is the standard presentation SL(2,Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6.

(3) Sign conventions. The signs are chosen so that:
- σ is the rotation by −π/2 of R^2 for the standard Euclidean structure;
- ρ is a rotation by −2π/6 for a suitable invariant metric.
The point Grothendieck stresses is that ρ and σ rotate in the same sense. Reinterpreted on bases (z_1, z_2) of lattices in C with z_1/z_2 ∈ D, the action of ρ and σ is 'positive': (z_k, u(z_k)) is a direct R-basis of C ≅ R^2, where u ∈ {ρ, σ}.

(4) Next he considers PD. This is apparently the circle bundle of normalized lattice bases over D, roughly D × S^1. Its universal cover is P\tilde D, roughly D × R. The group of all lifts of the SL(2,Z)-action on PD to P\tilde D is a canonical central extension \tilde{S}T_{11} of T_{11} = SL(2,Z) by Z. Its central generator ϖ acts by (τ, z) ↦ (τ, z+1).

In modern terms, this group is:
- the preimage of SL(2,Z) in the universal cover of SL(2,R);
- isomorphic to the braid group B_3, i.e. the mapping class group Γ_{1,1}^1 of the torus with one boundary component;
- the kernel Z is generated by Δ^4 = (σ_1σ_2)^6.

The purpose is to fix orientation conventions for lifting ρ and σ to the extension, presumably to obtain a presentation such as \tilde ρ^3 = \tilde σ^2 times a power of ϖ. This prepares the study of tangential base points, the Teichmüller tower in genus 1, and the Galois action on its fundamental groups.
errors: No mathematical errors found. ρ^3 = −1, σ^2 = −1 and σ^{-1} = −σ all check.
The rotation senses check: det(e_1, σe_1) < 0 and det(e_1, ρe_1) < 0, so both are clockwise, i.e. negative angles, as claimed.
The fixed point of τ ↦ 1/(1−τ) is indeed e^{iπ/3}, matching the figure.
Minor imprecision: 'u(z_1)' is not defined on the page. It must mean the component of u(z_1, z_2) for u = ρ or σ.
The exact definition of PD (presumably lattice bases modulo R_{>0}, i.e. D × S^1) is not stated on this page.

ideas.what: Presentation of SL(2,Z) by elliptic generators ρ (order 6, fixing j) and σ (order 4, fixing i), with ρ^3 = σ^2 = −1.
ideas.where_published: Implicit in the Esquisse d'un programme discussion of T_{1,1} and its 'building blocks'

ideas.what: Choosing signs so that both generators rotate in the same sense, i.e. act positively on oriented lattice bases.
ideas.modern_name: Orientation and sign conventions for lattice bases / the modular group

ideas.what: Central extension of SL(2,Z) by Z, obtained as the lifts of the action to the universal cover of the circle bundle over the half-plane, with central generator ϖ acting by translation.
ideas.modern_name: Preimage of SL(2,Z) in the universal cover of SL(2,R) ≅ braid group B_3 ≅ Γ_{1,1}^1 (torus with one boundary component)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Artin, Milnor; Birman–Hilden for the mapping-class interpretation)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the T_{1,1} level and tangential base points of the Teichmüller tower, but not this explicit construction

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful but standard conventions on generators of SL(2,Z) and on its canonical Z-central extension (B_3). It is useful context for Grothendieck's genus-one Teichmüller tower, but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'T_{11}' should be read as the Teichmüller group T_{1,1} (genus 1, one marked point).
The word inserted above the line before '\tilde{S}T_{11}' is plausibly 'canonique' (i.e. 'que l'on pourra écrire canoniquement ...'); the reading is uncertain.
In '(i.e. angle [?])' the bracketed word is illegible; possibly 'angle < 0' or 'angle négatif'.
'{+de j+}' is an insertion above the line: 'le groupe d'isotropie de j'.
P𝒟 / P\tilde{𝒟}: here 𝒟 denotes the upper half-plane (since z_1/z_2 ∈ 𝒟), and P𝒟 is presumably the circle bundle of normalized lattice bases.
